briefings.title: How the OBR will judge this Budget
briefings.headline: Headroom is a forecast. The OBR's typical five-year error is £33bn.

paragraphs.text: The OBR tests the stability rule on the current budget in the target year, the investment rule on whether net financial liabilities are falling as a share of GDP, and the welfare cap on capped spending against the cap and margin. It publishes its verdict with the Budget; the Chancellor may only suspend the rules in a significant shock, and the OBR judges whether one has occurred.

Headroom is a forecast, not a fact: the OBR's average absolute five-year forecast difference for receipts is 0.9% of GDP, about £33 billion by 2030-31. A Budget that passes by a few billion is one revision away from failing.

briefings.title: The estimate is not the OBR’s
briefings.headline: The economy here is our estimate, not the OBR’s. It publishes its own on 28 October.

paragraphs.text: The game plans on today’s estimate: the OBR’s March forecast with its own published sensitivities applied to today’s gilt yields and inflation. On 28 October the OBR will publish its own updated forecast; the arithmetic here shows what your Budget looks like if the estimate turns out to be right.
